gaps.text: In-line measurement of Broth temperature at the measuring point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: low-level fusion of the UV-Vis and Raman blocks, normalised so that neither block dominates the model, with one calibration kept per method. Both probes must look at the same small broth volume at the same time, and the two data streams must be brought to a common time step. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
Measuring Independent reference values for biomass and metabolites: The in-line signals are proxies, so calibration and the go/no-go decision need an independent laboratory value.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into one new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing a low-level fusion of UV-Vis and Raman blocks for O3, with the two blocks concatenated and normalised so neither dominates; the fused model should still be compared against the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general review, not a fermentation study, and it does not address same-volume sampling, common time steps, or probe alignment.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the source says it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution and complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the O3 go/no-go check: assess whether the Raman block adds complementary information to UV-Vis before keeping the second instrument, and drop it if the fused model does not beat the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review and does not specify UV-Vis/Raman, fermentation broth, or a low-level fusion workflow.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
